items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: sort of like – you’ve seen or you’ve heard some of Kurt Weill’s music – that idiom.

ctx.x: Did you meet any Russian jazz players?

Yes we did. We met a few. They played – their jazz was similar to what you heard during the ’20s and the ’30s. It was that kind of jazz, that real stiff kind of a thing, sort of like – you’ve seen or you’ve heard some of Kurt Weill’s music – that idiom. But they were really interested in everything we did, everything. I remember, we were down on a beach in Sochi. This Russian fellow came up to me. He was saying, “Look at this.” He said, “You see people all colors, every day,” he said, “not like the United…

I was infuriated by that, really furious, because I understood what he was doing. He was propagandizing, and more or less at our expense, and I wasn’t going to let that happen. I’m not anti-American or anything like that. I might resent discrimination that was more pervasive then than it was now, but I wouldn’t have let a guy get away with this. But they – an American reporter stopped the quotation at that point. I – to this day I resent it. I never met him. I don’t remember who he was, but if I were to run – to…
